clue.text: Sign of happy marriage — none of this

definitions.text: Sign of happy marriage — none of this

parts.note: surface reading: the token of a contented couple, a home without quarrels
setter's reading: 'this' is the very puzzle the solver holds, so the phrase also means not one puzzle of this kind

explanation.surface: A wistful remark on what proves a marriage is happy.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase describes a couple who never quarrel, and 'none of this' adds the joke that this crossword itself is what they never have.
explanation.definitionFit: Spouses who never exchange angry words are the classic picture of domestic bliss, and the pun on puzzles makes it self-referential.

clue.text: Old record player?

parts.note: surface reading: an antique machine for playing discs
setter's reading: split the word into an old single-channel recording format and the short name for a gramophone, though the whole word means interwoven initials

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the answer is read in two halves, MONO and GRAM (a gramophone), while the word itself means a design of a person's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken apart, the word is literally a single-channel gramophone, the kind of player found in an old household before stereo.

clue.text: Illness one may find in Africa

definitions.note: cryptic: something one may find in Africa, i.e. a country there

parts.note: mal is French for illness, familiar from grand mal and mal de mer
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A traveller's warning about a disease picked up on the African continent.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a landlocked West African republic, so it is literally a place one may find in that continent.

clue.text: Slow in raising one's hat to a politician

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something lifts it upwards, so its letters read bottom to top

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
taken as written
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone is tardy in doffing their hat to a passing MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory describes someone who delays or dawdles, so it is a formal synonym for tardy or sluggish.

clue.text: Island for a boy to cry over

parts.note: Les is a boy's name, short for Leslie

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the word is flipped end to end

parts.note: to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: A place where a little lad might weep his heart out.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesbos is a large Greek island in the north-east Aegean, home of the poet Sappho.

clue.text: Battle celebrated by Orange type

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Marlborough's 1704 victory over the French and Bavarians
second meaning: ... Orange is an old English variety of apple

explanation.surface: A victory commemorated by a Protestant Orangeman's parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orange' suggests the fruit or Ulster's Orange Order, but Blenheim Orange is a dessert apple, named for the palace built to celebrate the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The same place name labels the famous 1704 victory and an old English apple cultivar named after Marlborough's palace.

clue.text: Draw no conclusion from turning to the front

indicators.note: the result you get when the words are turned around, i.e. read backwards

parts.note: the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice not to read too much into an army's change of direction toward the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Onward means forward or ahead, the direction of the front, so it is a synonym of the adverbial phrase.

clue.text: It's not quite clear how a Jew almost managed to save Christian writings

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a Semite is a member of a people including Jews
to run a business is to manage it
to spare is to save or keep back
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A puzzled account of how a Jewish man nearly rescued some Christian manuscripts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something partly see-through lets light pass but not a sharp image, so it is not entirely clear.

clue.text: Bringing forth the case for the Euro?

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
the vocative is the grammatical case used to address someone

explanation.surface: Someone making the argument in favour of the single currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The case for' looks like an argument being made, but case is the grammatical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Evocative things call up memories or feelings, so the word means summoning or calling forth.

clue.text: Weapon whose abandonment may bring promotion

definitions.text: Weapon whose abandonment may bring promotion

parts.note: surface reading: a soldier throwing down his arms, which would hardly earn a reward
setter's reading: drop the spear's name from the front of a junior army rank and you are left with the next rank up

explanation.walkthrough: A lance corporal who loses the first word of the title becomes a full corporal, which is a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long cavalry spear, and the same word names the lowest non-commissioned grade in the British army.

clue.text: Porn appears for the first time in Beethoven's work

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: the Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the opening letter of time

explanation.surface: A shocking debut of smut in a classical masterpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is sexually explicit writing or art, a politer label for pornographic material.

clue.text: Ealing Broadway first confused Asian

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of Broadway

explanation.surface: A lost traveller from Asia muddled by the London Underground station Ealing Broadway.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing Broadway is a station in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bengali is a person from Bengal, in Bangladesh and eastern India, so an example of an Asian.

clue.text: Extent of territory occupied by Crusaders?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a unit of land area
second meaning: a port in present-day Israel held by the Crusaders

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one question about how much land the Crusaders held, but it splits into a unit of area and the city of Acre.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre measures land area, and Acre was a key Crusader fortress city on the Levantine coast.

clue.text: L could be a bargain

parts.note: setter's reading: the letter L heads a four-letter word for deficit, so it is that word's first letter
surface reading: a shop's cut-price offer

explanation.walkthrough: L is the leader of LOSS; a loss leader is an item sold below cost to lure shoppers in.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops price some goods below cost to draw customers who then buy other things, making those items bargains.

clue.text: One thing a spinster cannot do

definitions.text: One thing a spinster cannot do

parts.words: One thing a spinster cannot do
parts.note: surface reading: perhaps a woman who spins thread and her limits at the wheel
setter's reading: an unwed woman has never had a husband, so she cannot do it a second time

explanation.walkthrough: A spinster has never been wed, so she cannot wed again.
explanation.definitionFit: To do it again presupposes a first time, and a spinster by definition has never been a bride.

clue.text: Space traveller and model flier

parts.note: a red star, like any star, moves through space
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: An astronaut and a toy aeroplane taking to the skies.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird with a reddish tail, so it is one kind of flying creature.

clue.text: Tony provided plum duff for the family

definitions.note: first name standing for a character's surname

indicators.note: duff is British slang for faulty or broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A man named Tony brought a plum pudding for the relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Plum duff is a British steamed pudding, but duff here is the anagram signal. Tony Lumpkin is the loutish squire's son in Goldsmith's comedy She Stoops to Conquer.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename Tony points to Tony Lumpkin, the famous comic character in Goldsmith's eighteenth-century play.

clue.text: Substitute taking over key role

parts.note: surface reading: an understudy or reserve stepping into a leading part
setter's reading: the job of a door key, done instead by a burglar's tool

explanation.walkthrough: Key role sounds like a central part in a play or team, but it is literally what a key does.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar's thin tool opens locks without the proper key, doing that key's job in its place.

clue.text: Japanese growth threatening our country?

parts.note: surface reading: Japan's booming economy alarming British industry
setter's reading: an invasive plant from Japan that spreads through British gardens and damages buildings

explanation.walkthrough: Growth suggests the Japanese economy, but it is a plant. Japanese knotweed is a notorious invasive weed in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: This fast-spreading Asian plant is so destructive in Britain that it can block house sales and must be legally controlled.

clue.text: Effects lacking on our railways

parts.note: surface reading suggests consequences; setter's reading is the strip of film carrying the audio, including effects
setter's reading: a grumble that British rail lines are rarely in good condition

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as SOUND TRACK: a film's audio strip, and a rail line in good repair, which the setter jokes Britain lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A film's audio strip holds music and effects, and read as two words it is a well-maintained length of rail.

clue.text: Incompetent, but could be employed with a change of polarity

indicators.note: polarity switches between south and north poles, so one compass letter is swapped for the other

parts.note: able to be used

explanation.surface: A useless worker might still find a job if their attitude were reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the S (south pole) in USABLE for N (north pole).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lacks the ability to do something is not capable, which is what incompetent means.

clue.text: What a cat does with a rat

definitions.text: What a cat does with a rat

parts.words: What a cat does with a rat
parts.note: surface reading: the cat hunts, catches or plays with its prey
setter's reading: the words themselves, which share their ending sound

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a hunt, but the cat and rat are words: cat and rat end in the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Two words whose endings sound alike form a rhyme, as these two animal names plainly do.

clue.text: Nourishment available for two small coins

parts.note: padding: tells the solver that two separate coins are wanted
a sou was a French coin of little value
p is a penny

explanation.surface: A cheap meal on offer for a couple of coppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two small coins' means two different coins: the old French sou and a British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl of broth is food that sustains, so it is a form of nourishment.

clue.text: Why admit late items to be loaded?

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: broken into separate items, the letters lose their order and are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A query about why tardy goods should be put on the lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for having lots of money, so it is an informal synonym for rich.

clue.text: Relating to a period after privatising the mail

definitions.text: Relating to a period after privatising the mail

parts.note: surface reading: describing the era following some event
setter's reading: selling off the postal service would start a fight over it, a conflict about letters

explanation.walkthrough: The answer normally means after a war; split as POST WAR it is the battle the setter expects over privatising the Post Office.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the years following a conflict, and read in two words it is a quarrel over the post.

clue.text: What's wrong about party leader?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of party

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about what is amiss with a political chief.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: what many find wrong with a party leader is the media manipulation of spin doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is the slanted presentation of news by politicians' press handlers, a common complaint about party leaders.

clue.text: Authority for government measures

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sovereign or person who governs

definitions.note: verb; the answer is the thing that measures
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a straight-edged strip used for measuring lengths

explanation.surface: A body responsible for making government policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who governs is one sense, and a marked straight edge for drawing lines and measuring is the other.

clue.text: Dutch uncle without a notion of geometry

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one piece wraps around the other
Dutch suggests something foreign or double-Dutch gibberish, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
an idea is a notion

explanation.surface: A stern adviser who has no grasp of geometry.
explanation.walkthrough: A Dutch uncle is someone who lectures sternly, but 'Dutch' is the anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: The classical geometry of Euclid's Elements is the standard kind, so the adjective means relating to that geometry.
